submitted.rationale: Idx 14 (Sb 0.24, Y 0.76, near Y3SbO7) had the highest measured EQE, 2.7e-4 %. All predicted ternary and Y-oxide band gaps are above 2.7 eV, so every EQE in this system is near zero.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 1.4e-4 %. The Sb-rich end did not benefit from the low-gap Sb6O13 phase.
Measured EQE -8e-5 %, effectively zero. That's the Y-rich side, where wide-gap Y2O3 dominates.

consultations.verdict: Support: Y-rich ternary Y3SbO7 has HSE gap 3.6 eV and Sb5Y3O12 3.4 eV, both above 2.7 eV photons; only Sb-rich mixed-valence Sb6O13 (2.05 eV) absorbs at 2.7 eV. The Sb-richest candidate (idx 28) most likely contains the absorbing Sb-oxide phase.

Mixed: Y2O3 gap 5.6 eV argues against the Y-rich end absorbing 2.7 eV light. The Y2Sb2O7 prediction of 0.1 eV is probably wrong for a pyrochlore, so it tells us little. The Sb-rich end measured near zero, so I'm testing the middle, near Y3SbO7 (idx 14, Sb 0.24), to cover the line.

Uninformative to mildly supportive. Y3SbO7 is on the hull, so the Y-rich middle probably holds Y3SbO7 plus excess Y2O3. The measured EQE went up going from Sb-rich (idx 28) to idx 14, and the GP UCB points further Y-ward, to idx 9.
